rows.title: NFL wind: four Sunday totals to verify
rows.observation: The November 1 source selections are NE–MIA under 43.5 (-113), LAC–LAR under 45.5 (-111), ATL–TB under 43.5 (-111), and IND–JAX under 46.5 (-110). The screen uses average wind of at least 10 mph and temperatures from 33 to 90 degrees; displayed history is 635-467-10 with 11% ROI.
rows.interpretation: WATCH: these are source claims, not verified game-time weather effects. Stadium shelter and roof conditions can invalidate an outdoor weather proxy. Historical ROI is not a forecast for these four games.
rows.next_check: Verify venue, roof/open-air exposure and forecast near kickoff; compare the exact current total and price. Re-capture tomorrow before a new decision. No automatic wind adjustment.
rows.quote_status: Source-pick benchmark only; no verified executable sportsbook quote

rows.title: Portland–Utah: investigate the under
rows.observation: Action lists Under 232.5 at -112 as a system selection for October 31. Its displayed history is 534 wins, 434 losses, 9 pushes and 7% ROI. Filters include division games in the regular season, under support at 40% or less, and a total falling by at least one point from open to close.
rows.interpretation: WATCH: closing-line information is unavailable when an earlier ticket is placed. This is a third-party historical screen, not our calibrated win probability. The discovery row and expanded chart also disagree on total units; those units are not used.
rows.next_check: Compare the same sportsbook total at the actual decision time, verify line movement and current injuries/pace, then track an independent forward benchmark. Do not apply a fixed probability boost or copy the source stake.

rows.title: System discovery: win rate alone can mislead
rows.observation: The catalog includes both winning and losing historical screens. Its college-football Sharp Money screen shows 51% wins and -1% ROI; an MLB public-fade moneyline screen shows 59% wins and -3% ROI.
rows.interpretation: Use price-adjusted returns, sample size and forward results; neither a sharp-money label nor a high hit rate proves value. Selecting only the best historical screens risks selection bias.
rows.next_check: Keep source systems separate from agency results; test rules prospectively with timestamped inputs and realistic prices before changing betting behavior.

rows.title: College football: compare external model disagreements
rows.observation: At capture the dashboard displayed South Alabama +6.5 versus projection +2, Air Force +0.5 versus -3.5, and Kansas State +2.5 versus -1.2 for October 31 matchups. These are external model comparison leads, not accepted picks or verified book offers.
rows.interpretation: WATCH: a forecast disagreement identifies something to investigate. It does not establish which model is right. The dashboard supplies no named executable sportsbook for these displayed offers.
rows.next_check: Resolve full team/event identities and current sportsbook contracts, compare our forecast and injuries, and preserve the disagreement for later outcome scoring.

claude_reviews.summary: Top three observations (read-only; no code run; saved tests are for a different snapshot, so none certify this code). (1) Definite correctness risk, sportsbook.py:176-181 with evidence_decisions.py:67-69: the sb_decisions dedupe key mixes raw quotes with context.signature, which only changes on new evidence IDs/expiry. Edge/threshold decisions depend on belief() and agent state that are not hashed, so stale decisions can be reused or re-evaluated inconsistently; note signature also embeds time-dependent freshness booleans. (2) Probable selection/leakage-style inconsistency, sportsbook.py:187-195: the evidence layer can change the chosen book/side/line (selection_changed), yet 'changed' compares only against the best original-edge quote; when every option is blocked, sportsbook.py:191-192 falls back to `eligible or options` and still picks a blocked quote (rejected later via status, but the decision is logged against it). Also evidence_decisions.py:98-100 blocks on any non-active injury row without name/team checks, and the injury hypothesis path (evidence_decisions.py:102) only inspects [:1] hypotheses per key, so a stale newest row masks a valid older one. Research context also flags unverified teammate links; the code checks source player status but not roster relationship. (3) Unsafe-ish accounting/calibration: stake cap of .5*unit when probability changes (evidence_decisions.py:88) combined with the min-stake gate `stake>=.5*a['unit']` (sportsbook.py:204) is fine, but the 'edge' used for acceptance (sportsbook.py:187-189) is p-1/decimal(price), ignoring vig/push probability for spread/total, and belief() normal-error sigma (sportsbook.py:125) is uncalibrated, so thresholds of 1-2 points are not meaningfully calibrated. WEIGHTS are explicitly unfitted hypotheses. Missing validation: no test of double adjustment (belief bias plus evidence blend) or of settlement of pushes on quarter lines (filtered at load, sportsbook.py:58).

Top three observations (proposals for human review; I did not run code). (1) Definite stability bug, news_hypotheses.py:117-118: when model is None, `edge` is None, but the action expression evaluates `'WATCH' if model is None else 'SHADOW_CANDIDATE' if edge>=.02 else 'PASS'` and is safe only because of ordering; however line 110 selects q via options where p is None gives -1, and line 105 hypothesis() can return (None, reason) so `model['revised']` is guarded, yet teams_history[team] (line 105) raises KeyError if the team has no history slice, which is uncaught inside the transaction and would abort the whole tick. (2) Temporal/selection concern, news_hypotheses.py:54 and 49: the shrunk minutes change uses the post-teammate-appearance sample including games with future-of-baseline overlap (own is tail(30) before today so no leakage), but the injury snapshot is only freshness-checked (4h) not timestamped against the quote time, and the best-edge quote across books/sides is selected after seeing the model (lines 107-110), then gap>=.02 labels SHADOW_CANDIDATE; this is max-over-options selection bias that inflates candidate_units in public() (line 147). Brier scoring (line 131) treats pushes as None but win/loss for the chosen side only; calibration is unvalidated at the 0.02 threshold. (3) context_trends.py:29-34 selects the book-specific quote per past game with max observed_utc, fine for leakage, but line 85 picks the book via min(book) alphabetically rather than the best/current line, and line 24 compares int(r.team_id) which can raise ValueError on NaN/non-numeric ids and abort the transaction (no per-player try/except). Also line 74-75 builds by_quote_player keyed by pid but quotes may carry zero-padded or differently typed player_ids; identity mismatch silently yields all-unknown rows. Passing tests are synthetic and do not certify forecast quality.

bankroll_policy: New paper stakes: at most 40% committed overall, 10% per sport, 2% per game and 1% per ticket. At most 10% committed beyond 24 hours. Sportsbook NBA/NFL game lines may use 7.5% per sport, leaving 2.5% of bankroll for props within the 10% sport limit. Percentages use the lower of initial bankroll and current cash plus open stakes; profits do not automatically increase limits. Existing locked tickets remain intact, and may exceed new limits until settlement. Model and sportsbook accounts stay separate.
